text:
alex: Quick sync — trying to finalize TTFT + tok/s normalization for the new perf dashboard. Need quick decisions on sampling window (10k requests vs 1h sliding), whether tok/s should be normalized by generated tokens only (exclude prompt), and whether p95 should be computed on raw per-request TTFT or on per-token rates. cc @maria @devon @irene. Goal: ship panel changes by EOD Wed. PR will follow.
maria: My take — dashboard panels use 1h sliding windows (smoother for UI), alerts use count-based windows (10k requests or 5m whichever hits first). Normalize tok/s by generated output tokens only. Exclude prompt tokens from throughput numbers. :thumbsup:
devon: For regressions/alerts: compute p95 on per-request TTFT (first-token latency) so it's intuitive for devs. Keep tok/s p50/p95 exposed separately for throughput trends. Also add per-model + per-route grouping. Important: exclude cached-prefix hits from TTFT alerting (they artificially lower p95). I'll open a bench to validate assumptions.
sam: FYI kicked off a quick bench job against staging for the three sample models.
benchbot: bench-run 3247 completed: sampled 2,000 requests across models [rwd-base, rwd-compact, rwd-large]. Summary: TTFT p95 = 210ms / 310ms / 450ms, tok/s p95 = 65 / 48 / 30. Cache hit rate = 12%. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/bench/3247
irene: For panels I'd prefer promQL-based derivations so we can reuse existing dashboards. Current metric names: first_token_latency_ms{model,route,cache_hit} and tokens_per_sec{model,route}. Proposed queries:

```promql
# TTFT p95 per model (1h sliding)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(first_token_latency_ms_bucket[1h])) by (le, model))

# tok/s p95 per model (1h sliding)
quantile_over_time(0.95, tokens_per_sec[1h]) by (model)
```

And alert snippet for TTFT (count-based window):

```yaml
alert: TTFT_P95_Latency
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(first_token_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route)) > 300
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "TTFT p95 > 300ms for {{ $labels.model }} / {{ $labels.route }}"
```

alex: Ack. @devon can you make a tiny PR to add metric labels (route_id not full path, model, cache_hit) and add a note about excluding cached requests from the TTFT alert query? Also add a 'sample_rate' telemetry label so bench runs can be normalized across jobs. Ping me when ready.
devon: Will do. Quick question — route_id vs route_name: route_id minimizes cardinality. Also want to confirm we want to store both prompt_tokens and gen_tokens as fields so we can compute normalized tok/s later. If yes I'll add them.
maria: +1 for route_id and storing prompt_tokens & gen_tokens. That helps slicing by client dataset too. Add dataset label on dashboard table.
sam: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/842 "metrics: add labels + dashboard updates (ttft, tok/s)". Small changes: add route_id label, add prompt_tokens/gen_tokens counters, expose cache_hit boolean.
alex: Reviewing now — will comment inline and merge after a quick perf sanity check from devon. Thanks everyone. :eyes:
